note: §17.558 — goldens for score_research.py. Each topic supplies collected `entries` (the synthesis input) + `expected_facets` (coverage targets, §17.550 AND-substring shape). The eval drives _generate_summary over the entries, then scores COVERAGE (facets addressed) + GROUNDING (faithfulness of the summary against the entries). Entries are real factual content so grounding is meaningful; a good summary should cover the facets AND stay grounded (no fabricated claims).

entries.content: The 8086 uses a segmented memory model. A 20-bit physical address is formed by shifting the 16-bit segment register left by 4 bits and adding the 16-bit offset, giving access to a 1 MB address space from 16-bit registers.

INT 21h is the primary DOS API interrupt. The AH register selects the function: 01h reads a character, 02h writes a character, 09h prints a '$'-terminated string, and 4Ch terminates the program. Parameters are passed in registers.
INT 16h provides BIOS keyboard services. AH=00h blocks until a keystroke is available and returns the scan code in AH and the ASCII code in AL. AH=01h checks keyboard status without blocking.

Real mode uses segment:offset addressing limited to 1 MB. Protected mode, introduced on the 80286, adds descriptor tables, four privilege rings, and access to extended memory beyond 1 MB, forming the basis of modern multitasking operating systems.

Hybrid search combines a dense vector leg (semantic embeddings) with a sparse lexical leg (BM25 term scoring) and fuses the two rank lists with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), which is robust to differing score scales between the legs.

A cross-encoder reranker jointly encodes the query and each candidate document to produce a relevance score. It is more accurate than bi-encoder retrieval but quadratically more expensive, so it is applied only to the top-k candidates returned by first-stage retrieval.

Document chunking trades recall against precision: small chunks improve precision but fragment context, while overlap between adjacent chunks preserves cross-boundary context at the cost of some redundancy in the index.

goldens.topic: analog active and passive filter design

entries.content: A Sallen-Key filter is a second-order active filter topology using a single op-amp. The low-pass variant places two resistors and two capacitors around the op-amp to set the cutoff frequency and Q, giving a 2-pole (40 dB/decade) rolloff.

A first-order passive RC low-pass filter is a single resistor and capacitor; its cutoff frequency is f = 1 / (2*pi*R*C) and it rolls off at 20 dB/decade. It needs no power supply but cannot provide gain and loads the source impedance.

A multiple-feedback (MFB) band-pass filter passes a band of frequencies between a low and a high cutoff, attenuating signals outside the band. Its center frequency and bandwidth are set by the feedback resistor and capacitor network around the op-amp.
